facts.title: The Word 'Ignite' is Ancient!
facts.fact: The Sanskrit word 'Agni' (अग्नि - fire) shares the same Indo-European root as Latin 'ignis', which gave us English 'ignite' and 'ignition'. After 3,500 years, we're still using essentially the same word for fire!
facts.shareText: 🔥 Did you know? 'Ignite' comes from the ancient Sanskrit 'Agni' - same word, 3,500 years later!

facts.title: Ancient Existential Questions
facts.fact: The Nasadiya Sukta (Hymn 10.129) ends with radical intellectual honesty: 'Who really knows? Who can say? Perhaps it formed itself, or perhaps it did not.' 3,500 years ago, Vedic sages were already questioning the origins of existence with scientific skepticism!
facts.shareText: 💭 Ancient wisdom: The Rig Veda asked 'Who really knows?' about creation - ultimate intellectual humility!

facts.title: Indra: The Original Superhero
facts.fact: Indra has 289 hymns dedicated to him - more than any other deity! He's the original 'superhero' who defeats demons, releases waters, and drinks soma to power up before battles. Think Thor meets Superman!
facts.shareText: ⚡ Indra: 289 hymns strong - the OG superhero of ancient texts!

facts.title: Ancient Astronomy
facts.fact: Hymn 1.164 describes the solar year using the metaphor of a wheel with 12 spokes (months) and 360 points (days). The ancient Vedic people had remarkably accurate astronomical knowledge and encoded it in poetry!
facts.shareText: 🌟 Ancient Indians encoded the 360-day calendar in poetry 3,500 years ago!

facts.title: The Inseparable Trio
facts.fact: Ushas (Dawn) appears in 20 hymns, but she's ALWAYS mentioned alongside the Ashvins (twin gods). They're like an ancient divine trio that never separates - the Ashvins ride a golden chariot that brings Ushas across the sky each morning.
facts.shareText: 🌅 Dawn goddess Ushas never appears alone - always with her twin companions, the Ashvins!

facts.title: Father Sky, Mother Earth
facts.fact: The Sanskrit 'Dyaus Pitar' (Sky Father) is linguistically identical to Greek 'Zeus Pater' and Latin 'Jupiter'. Same god, same name, spread across ancient Indo-European cultures!
facts.shareText: ⚡ Zeus, Jupiter, and Dyaus are literally the SAME god with the same name in different languages!

facts.title: The Question That Has No Answer
facts.fact: The Rig Veda contains the Riddle Hymn (1.164) with 52 verses of cryptic questions about existence, consciousness, and reality. It asks: 'What holds up the universe? What is the foundation of thought?' - questions we're still pondering!
facts.shareText: 🤔 The Rig Veda asked 'What is the foundation of thought?' 3,500 years before neuroscience!

facts.title: The God Who Got Promoted
facts.fact: The Ribhus were originally skilled craftsmen who became gods through their exceptional artistry! They created miraculous objects and were granted immortality as a reward. Talk about career advancement!
facts.shareText: 🔨 The Ribhus worked their way UP to becoming gods - divine career goals!

facts.title: Soma: Ancient Psychedelic?
facts.fact: Scholars have debated for over a century what the mysterious soma plant actually was. Theories include: ephedra, cannabis, fly agaric mushroom, or even a lost species. The ancient recipe remains one of history's greatest mysteries!
facts.shareText: 🍄 What was soma? The ancient psychedelic recipe has been lost for 3,000+ years!

facts.title: The Dynamic Duo
facts.fact: Indra and Agni are mentioned together in 157 hymns - the most frequently paired deities in the entire Rig Veda! Agni (fire) carries offerings up, Indra (thunder) brings rain down. The ultimate collaboration!
facts.shareText: 🔥⚡ Indra + Agni: 157 hymns together - the original power couple!

facts.title: First Feminist Theology?
facts.fact: Hymn 10.125 is spoken by Vac (Speech) herself - a goddess declaring her own supremacy: 'I am the Queen, I am the gatherer-up of treasures.' This is one of the earliest examples of a female deity speaking in first person!
facts.shareText: 👑 Goddess Vac declares: 'I am the Queen' - ancient female empowerment!

facts.title: The Battle That Created Rivers
facts.fact: Indra's most famous deed was slaying Vritra, a cosmic serpent/demon who was hoarding all the world's waters. When Indra killed him, the waters were released, creating rivers and bringing life to earth. Epic cosmic plumbing!
facts.shareText: ⚡ Indra defeated a dragon to release all the world's waters - ultimate hero moment!

facts.title: The Ancient Word for 'Honey'
facts.fact: The Sanskrit word 'madhu' (honey/sweet) gave us 'mead' in English. The same root appears in Greek 'methy' (wine) and Old English 'meodu'. Sweet things have been sweet for millennia!
facts.shareText: 🍯 'Mead' and 'madhu' (honey) - same sweet word for 4,000 years!

facts.title: Counting in Ancient Times
facts.fact: The Rig Veda uses large numbers like 'sahasra' (thousand) and 'ayuta' (ten thousand) frequently, showing sophisticated mathematical concepts. They describe armies of 100,000 and cosmic time spans reaching into millions!
facts.shareText: 🔢 Ancient Vedic people counted in thousands and millions - serious math!

facts.title: The Goddess Who Never Ages
facts.fact: Ushas (Dawn) is described as 'ever-young' because she renews herself every morning. While countless generations grow old and die, Dawn remains eternally youthful - the original immortal beauty!
facts.shareText: 🌅 Dawn never ages - she's been young for 3,500+ years!

facts.title: Mitra-Varuna: Two Sides of One Coin
facts.fact: Mitra and Varuna are so frequently invoked together that they're often treated as a divine pair (Mitra-Varuna). Mitra rules day and friendship; Varuna rules night and cosmic law. Think Batman and Superman of the ancient world!
facts.shareText: ☀️🌙 Mitra (day) & Varuna (night) - the original dynamic duo!

facts.title: The Concept of Rita
facts.fact: 'Rita' (ऋत) is cosmic order, truth, and natural law all rolled into one. It's the fundamental principle that keeps the universe functioning. Breaking rita causes chaos; following it brings harmony. The Force before Star Wars!
facts.shareText: ⚖️ Rita: Ancient concept of cosmic order - the universe's operating system!

facts.title: The Noose of Justice
facts.fact: Varuna catches sinners with his magical noose (pasha). If you break an oath or commit a sin, Varuna's noose will find you. He's basically the original cosmic detective with a lasso of truth!
facts.shareText: 🪢 Varuna catches sinners with a magical noose - ancient justice system!

facts.title: Seven Rivers Mystery
facts.fact: The Rig Veda frequently mentions 'sapta sindhu' (seven rivers). Scholars debate which rivers these are, but they're central to Vedic geography. The entire civilization was defined by these waterways!
facts.shareText: 🌊 The 'seven rivers' of the Rig Veda - ancient geography mystery!

facts.title: God = Deva = Divine
facts.fact: The Sanskrit 'deva' (god) comes from the root 'div' meaning 'to shine'. Gods are literally 'shining ones'. This root gives us 'divine', 'deity', and even 'Tuesday' (Tiw's day, from Germanic *Tiwaz, related to Sanskrit dyaus)!
facts.shareText: ✨ 'Deva' means 'shining one' - gods were literally beings of light!

facts.title: Soma: The Drink of Immortality
facts.fact: Soma wasn't just any drink - it was believed to grant immortality (amrita). The gods themselves drank it to maintain their divine status. In later mythology, gods and demons fought a cosmic war over it!
facts.shareText: 🍷 Soma granted immortality - the ancient elixir of life!

facts.title: Mind vs. Heart Ancient Debate
facts.fact: The Rig Veda distinguishes between 'manas' (processing mind), 'hridaya' (heart/emotional center), and 'chitta' (pure consciousness). This psychological model predates Western philosophy by millennia!
facts.shareText: 🧠 Ancient Indians had different words for mind, consciousness, and heart-center!

facts.title: Agni: The Ultimate Messenger
facts.fact: Agni appears in 218 hymns and is connected to nearly every other deity. Why? He's the messenger who carries offerings from humans to gods. He's literally the divine postal service!
facts.shareText: 📬 Agni is the divine messenger - ancient spiritual post office!

facts.title: Poetic Meters as Code
facts.fact: The Rig Veda uses sophisticated poetic meters (chandas) like Gayatri (24 syllables), Trishtubh (44 syllables), and Jagati (48 syllables). These weren't just for beauty - they were mnemonic devices to preserve accuracy across generations!
facts.shareText: 📖 Ancient Indians used poetic meter as data compression - 3,500 years before computers!

facts.title: The Twins Who Save Everyone
facts.fact: The Ashvins are divine physicians who rescue shipwrecked sailors, restore sight to the blind, and even give youth back to the elderly. They're basically ancient superheroes with a medical license!
facts.shareText: 🐎 The Ashvins: Divine doctors who rescued drowning sailors and restored youth!

facts.title: The First Gender-Neutral Pronoun?
facts.fact: The Rig Veda uses 'tad ekam' (That One) to refer to the ultimate reality before creation - neither male nor female, neither being nor non-being. Non-binary divinity 3,500 years ago!
facts.shareText: ♾️ The Rig Veda describes ultimate reality as 'That One' - beyond gender!

facts.title: The Ancient Word for 'Mother'
facts.fact: Sanskrit 'matar' (mother) is nearly identical across Indo-European languages: Latin 'mater', Greek 'meter', Old English 'modor', Persian 'madar'. The word for 'mother' has barely changed in 6,000 years!
facts.shareText: 👩‍👧 'Mother' sounds almost the same in 50+ languages - oldest word ever!

facts.title: Vishnu's Three Steps
facts.fact: In the Rig Veda, Vishnu takes three cosmic steps that measure the entire universe. First step: Earth. Second step: Atmosphere. Third step: Heaven. He literally walked across creation!
facts.shareText: 🦶 Vishnu measured the universe in 3 steps - ultimate stride!

facts.title: Ancient Acoustics
facts.fact: The Rig Veda was composed to be recited aloud with specific pitch accents (svara). These accents were so important that they were preserved through 3,500 years of oral transmission with stunning accuracy!
facts.shareText: 🎵 The Rig Veda was sung with specific pitches - preserved for 3,500 years!

facts.title: The Family Business
facts.fact: Many hymns were composed by specific family lineages! The Atris composed much of Mandala 5, the Vishvamitras did Mandala 3, and the Kanvas did Mandala 8. Vedic poetry was a family tradition passed down through generations!
facts.shareText: 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Rig Vedic hymns were family businesses - poetic dynasties!

facts.title: First Recorded Doubt
facts.fact: The Nasadiya Sukta (10.129) is perhaps the first recorded expression of metaphysical doubt. The poet admits that even the gods might not know how creation began. Radical honesty in ancient theology!
facts.shareText: ❓ 'Perhaps even the gods don't know' - ancient admission of uncertainty!

facts.title: Rudra: The Healer Who Hurts
facts.fact: Rudra is simultaneously feared as a bringer of disease and praised as a healer. He has a thousand medicines but also a thousand arrows. The original embodiment of 'what doesn't kill you makes you stronger'!
facts.shareText: ⚕️ Rudra: God of both disease AND healing - ultimate paradox!

facts.title: The Number Seven is Sacred
facts.fact: The number seven appears everywhere in the Rig Veda: seven rivers, seven sages (rishis), seven rays of Agni, seven waters. The mystical significance of seven dates back at least 3,500 years!
facts.shareText: 7️⃣ Seven rivers, seven sages, seven rays - ancient sacred number!

facts.title: Oral Tradition Accuracy
facts.fact: The Rig Veda was transmitted orally for nearly 2,000 years before being written down, yet scholars confirm it remained virtually unchanged. Ancient memory techniques were incredibly sophisticated!
facts.shareText: 🗣️ 2,000 years of oral transmission with ZERO changes - human memory at its peak!

facts.title: The Gambler's Lament
facts.fact: Hymn 10.34 is a moving plea from a gambling addict to stop playing dice! It's one of the most relatable and human hymns, showing that addiction struggles existed 3,500 years ago.
facts.shareText: 🎲 Ancient hymn about gambling addiction - some struggles are timeless!

facts.title: The Power of Intention
facts.fact: The concept of 'sankalpa' (intention/will) appears in the Rig Veda. The idea that focused intention shapes reality is ancient wisdom now backed by modern psychology!
facts.shareText: 💭 'Sankalpa' (intention) shapes reality - 3,500-year-old law of attraction!

facts.title: Heaven and Earth: The Original Couple
facts.fact: Dyaus (Sky Father) and Prithivi (Earth Mother) are invoked together 56 times - they're the cosmic parents who created everything. Think Greek Ouranos and Gaia, but earlier!
facts.shareText: 🌍☁️ Sky Father + Earth Mother = Everything. Ancient cosmic romance!

facts.title: The Dialogue Hymns
facts.fact: Some hymns are actual dramatic dialogues! The most famous is between Yama (Death) and his twin sister Yami - a moving conversation about mortality and loss. Ancient theater!
facts.shareText: 🎭 The Rig Veda has dialogue hymns - ancient drama in verse!

facts.title: Water Purification Rituals
facts.fact: The Rig Veda describes waters as 'ghrtavat' (mixed with ghee/clarifying agent) for purification. Ancient water treatment techniques encoded in religious rituals!
facts.shareText: 💧 Ancient water purification techniques disguised as religious rituals!

facts.title: Name Yourself
facts.fact: The Sanskrit word 'nama' (name) gives us 'name' in English, 'nomen' in Latin, 'onoma' in Greek. Humans have been naming things the same way for millennia!
facts.shareText: 📛 'Name' has been 'nama' for 5,000+ years - literally!

facts.title: The Word 'Veda' Itself
facts.fact: Sanskrit 'Veda' (वेद - knowledge) shares its root with English 'wit', Latin 'video' (I see), and Russian 'vedat' (to know). Knowledge and vision were literally the same concept in ancient times!
facts.shareText: 🧠 'Veda' (knowledge) and 'video' (I see) come from the same ancient root!

facts.title: The Ancient Word for 'New'
facts.fact: Sanskrit 'nava' (new) gives us 'novel', 'novice', 'innovate', and even 'November' (originally 9th month of new year). Newness has stayed new for 5,000 years!
facts.shareText: ✨ 'Novel' and 'nava' (new) - same word across 50 centuries!

facts.title: Sacred Sound 'OM'
facts.fact: The sacred syllable 'OM' (ॐ) appears in the Rig Veda as the primordial sound. Modern physicists note that 'Om' resonates at 432 Hz - the same frequency as Earth's natural vibration!
facts.shareText: 🕉️ OM resonates at Earth's natural frequency - ancient science!

facts.title: Brother From Another Mother
facts.fact: Sanskrit 'bhrater' (brother) is nearly identical to English 'brother', German 'bruder', Russian 'brat', and Persian 'baradar'. Brotherhood has been universal for millennia!
facts.shareText: 👬 'Brother' sounds the same in 40+ languages - ancient family tie!

facts.title: Wheel of Time
facts.fact: Sanskrit 'chakra' (wheel) became 'cycle' in English via Greek 'kyklos'. The Rig Veda's metaphor of time as a turning wheel literally shaped our language!
facts.shareText: ⚙️ 'Cycle' comes from Sanskrit 'chakra' (wheel) - circular etymology!

facts.title: The Ancient Word for 'Path'
facts.fact: Sanskrit 'patha' (path) gives us 'path' in English, 'pathos' in Greek, and 'pista' in Russian. Roads have been roads forever!
facts.shareText: 🛤️ 'Path' has literally been the same word for 6,000 years!

facts.title: Sacred Sound of 'S'
facts.fact: Sanskrit sibilant 's' sound was considered sacred and appears in divine names: Surya, Soma, Sarasvati, Savitar. Ancient sound symbolism!
facts.shareText: 🔊 The 'S' sound was sacred in ancient times - divine sibilance!

facts.title: The First Multiverse Theory
facts.fact: Hymn 10.90 describes the cosmic being Purusha being sacrificed to create multiple worlds. Ancient many-worlds interpretation 3,500 years before quantum physics!
facts.shareText: 🌌 The Rig Veda described multiple worlds 3,500 years ago - ancient multiverse!

facts.title: Consciousness Precedes Matter
facts.fact: The Rig Veda suggests consciousness (chit) existed before the material universe. This idealist philosophy predates Western idealism by 3,000 years!
facts.shareText: 🧠 Ancient wisdom: Consciousness came before matter!

facts.title: The Debt We Owe
facts.fact: The Rig Veda describes three debts (rna) humans are born with: to gods, to sages, and to ancestors. Life itself is a gift requiring repayment through ritual, study, and family!
facts.shareText: ⚖️ Ancient philosophy: You're born with three debts to repay!

facts.title: Unity in Diversity
facts.fact: The famous verse 'Ekam sat vipra bahudha vadanti' means 'Truth is one, the wise call it by many names.' Religious pluralism 3,500 years before modern tolerance movements!
facts.shareText: ☮️ 'Truth is one, names are many' - ancient religious tolerance!

facts.title: The Mind Creates Reality
facts.fact: The Rig Veda states 'yad bhavam tad bhavati' - as you think, so you become. The law of attraction was ancient wisdom before modern self-help!
facts.shareText: 🎯 'As you think, so you become' - 3,500-year-old manifestation!

facts.title: Non-Dualism Seeds
facts.fact: While later Vedanta developed non-dualism fully, the Rig Veda contains seeds of this philosophy when it asks: 'What was the One breathing breathlessly?'
facts.shareText: ♾️ The One breathing breathlessly - ancient non-dual wisdom!

facts.title: Sacrifice as Transformation
facts.fact: The concept of 'yajna' (sacrifice) in the Rig Veda isn't just ritual - it's the principle that transformation requires giving something up. Ancient understanding of opportunity cost!
facts.shareText: 🔥 Ancient wisdom: All transformation requires sacrifice!

facts.title: Agni's Three Forms
facts.fact: Agni manifests in three realms: as fire on earth, as lightning in the atmosphere, and as the sun in heaven. Same god, triple manifestation!
facts.shareText: 🔥⚡☀️ Agni is fire on earth, lightning in sky, sun in heaven - triple threat!

facts.title: The Night Goddess
facts.fact: Ratri (Night) is praised in one of the most beautiful hymns as both protective and potentially dangerous. She's the original 'dark but lovely' goddess!
facts.shareText: 🌙 Ratri (Night) is both protective mother and lurking danger!

facts.title: Sarasvati: The Lost River
facts.fact: Sarasvati was both a goddess AND a mighty river that mysteriously dried up around 1900 BCE. Satellite imagery now confirms an ancient river bed matching the Rig Vedic descriptions!
facts.shareText: 🌊 Goddess Sarasvati was a real river that vanished 4,000 years ago!

facts.title: The Craftsman God
facts.fact: Tvashtar is the divine craftsman who forges Indra's thunderbolt weapon. He's the ancient equivalent of Hephaestus/Vulcan - divine blacksmith!
facts.shareText: 🔨 Tvashtar forged Indra's thunderbolt - divine craftsman!

facts.title: Pushan: The Lost and Found God
facts.fact: Pushan is the deity of roads, journeys, and lost things. Ancient travelers prayed to him before setting out. The original patron saint of travelers!
facts.shareText: 🧭 Pushan helps find lost things - ancient GPS god!

facts.title: The Storm Warriors
facts.fact: The Maruts are warrior gods who ride on storm clouds with golden weapons and brazen armor. They're Indra's battle companions - ancient super-soldier squad!
facts.shareText: ⛈️ The Maruts: Storm warrior gods riding golden chariots!

facts.title: Parjanya: The Rain Bringer
facts.fact: Parjanya is praised for fertilizing the earth with rain. Farmers would sing hymns to him for good harvests. Ancient weather manipulation prayers!
facts.shareText: 🌧️ Parjanya brings rain and fertility - ancient rainmaker!

facts.title: The Divine Waters
facts.fact: Apas (Waters) are personified as goddesses who purify, heal, and grant wishes. Water worship in the Rig Veda predates all major religions!
facts.shareText: 💧 Waters are divine goddesses in the Rig Veda!

facts.title: Aditi: The Infinite Mother
facts.fact: Aditi represents boundless space and infinite nature - she's literally called 'the infinite one'. Mother of gods, personification of eternity!
facts.shareText: ♾️ Aditi means 'infinite' - mother of all gods!

facts.title: The Cosmic Horse Sacrifice
facts.fact: The Ashvamedha (horse sacrifice) ritual described in the Rig Veda symbolized royal power. A consecrated horse would roam free for a year, and wherever it went became the king's domain!
facts.shareText: 🐎 Ancient kings expanded territory by letting a sacred horse roam free!

facts.title: Brihaspati: Lord of Prayer
facts.fact: Brihaspati is the deity of devotion and prayer itself. He later became Guru (Jupiter) in astrology. The original spiritual teacher!
facts.shareText: 🙏 Brihaspati is the god OF prayer - meta-devotion!

facts.title: Soma Pavamana
facts.fact: 'Pavamana' means 'purifying oneself'. Mandala 9 is entirely dedicated to soma purifying itself through the filter - 114 hymns of ancient chemistry!
facts.shareText: 🍷 114 hymns describe soma filtering itself - ancient distillation!

facts.title: Ancient Hydrological Cycle
facts.fact: The Rig Veda describes how waters evaporate, form clouds, and return as rain. Complete understanding of the water cycle 3,500 years ago!
facts.shareText: ☁️💧 Ancient Indians understood the complete water cycle!

facts.title: Decimal System Origins
facts.fact: The Rig Veda uses powers of ten systematically: dasa (10), shata (100), sahasra (1000), ayuta (10,000). The decimal system was born here!
facts.shareText: 🔢 The decimal system originated in Rig Vedic mathematics!

facts.title: Soma's Chemical Properties
facts.fact: The Rig Veda describes soma as golden-colored, pressed through cloth filters, mixed with milk or water, and having intoxicating properties. Detailed ancient pharmacology!
facts.shareText: 🧪 Soma's preparation was detailed ancient chemistry!

facts.title: Embryology References
facts.fact: Hymn 10.184 contains prayers for pregnancy and describes fetal development. Ancient understanding of reproduction!
facts.shareText: 👶 The Rig Veda describes fetal development - ancient biology!

facts.title: Speed of Light Hint
facts.fact: While not explicit, some scholars interpret hymn 1.50.4 as describing the sun's rays reaching earth 'in a wink' (nimesha). Poetic understanding of light speed?
facts.shareText: ☀️ Did ancient Indians know light travels fast? Possible reference in Rig Veda!

facts.title: Medicinal Plant Knowledge
facts.fact: The Rig Veda mentions over 60 plants with medicinal properties. Ancient herbal pharmacopoeia preserved in verse!
facts.shareText: 🌿 60+ medicinal plants catalogued in ancient poetry!

facts.title: Surya-Savitar Mystery
facts.fact: Surya and Savitar are both solar deities, but Surya is the visible sun while Savitar is the sun's spiritual power. Same celestial body, different aspects!
facts.shareText: ☀️ Two sun gods: Surya (visible) and Savitar (spiritual power)!

facts.title: The Triad of Fire
facts.fact: Agni, Indra, and Surya form a triad representing three aspects of light: fire, lightning, and sun. The divine light spectrum!
facts.shareText: 🔥⚡☀️ Fire-Lightning-Sun: Ancient light triad!

facts.title: Soma and Moon Connection
facts.fact: Soma later became identified with the moon (Chandra). The bright juice of soma paralleled the bright face of the moon. Celestial-botanical fusion!
facts.shareText: 🌙🍷 Soma (divine drink) became the Moon - ancient fusion!

facts.title: The Feminine Divine Trinity
facts.fact: Ushas (Dawn), Ratri (Night), and Sarasvati (River) represent flowing feminine energies in the Rig Veda. Ancient goddess power!
facts.shareText: 🌅🌙🌊 Dawn-Night-River: Feminine divine trinity!

facts.title: Rudra-Maruts Father-Sons
facts.fact: Rudra is the father of the Maruts (storm gods). His fierce nature is multiplied in his warrior sons. Divine genetics!
facts.shareText: ⛈️ Rudra's sons are the storm warriors - divine family!

facts.title: Heaven and Earth's Children
facts.fact: The gods are called 'sons of heaven and earth' (dyava-prithivi putra). All divine beings emerged from the cosmic parents!
facts.shareText: 🌍☁️ All gods are children of Sky and Earth!

facts.title: The Sacred Cow
facts.fact: The cow (gau) is praised in 723 hymns! She represents wealth, nourishment, and the earth itself. The ancient sacred bovine!
facts.shareText: 🐄 The cow appears in 723 hymns - ultimate sacred animal!

facts.title: Yama's First Death
facts.fact: Yama was the first mortal to die and thus became lord of the dead. He literally pioneered death so others would have a path to follow!
facts.shareText: 💀 Yama was the FIRST person to die - original death pioneer!

facts.title: The Divine Horse
facts.fact: Horses (ashva) were so sacred that hymn 1.162 praises a single horse for 22 verses! Ancient horse worship!
facts.shareText: 🐎 22 verses praising a single horse - ultimate equine respect!

facts.title: The Cosmic Serpent
facts.fact: Ahi (serpent) appears as both enemy (Vritra) and symbol of water/fertility. Snakes were complex symbols - not just evil!
facts.shareText: 🐍 Ancient serpents were complex - both creative and destructive!

facts.title: The Four Goals of Life
facts.fact: While fully developed later, the Rig Veda hints at dharma (duty), artha (prosperity), kama (pleasure), and moksha (liberation) as life's aims!
facts.shareText: 🎯 Four life goals: Duty, Wealth, Pleasure, Liberation!

facts.title: The Concept of Tapas
facts.fact: 'Tapas' (heat/austerity) is described as the power that created the universe! Cosmic heat = creative force. Ancient thermodynamics?
facts.shareText: 🔥 Heat (tapas) created the universe - ancient energy theory!

facts.title: Vision Creates Gods
facts.fact: The Rig Veda states that the 'poets created the gods through their vision' (kavi). Divine beings emerged from human imagination!
facts.shareText: 👁️ Poets created gods through vision - ancient creative theology!

facts.title: Speech is Power
facts.fact: The goddess Vac (Speech) is described as the source of all power. Words literally create reality in Vedic thought!
facts.shareText: 🗣️ Speech (Vac) creates reality - ancient power of words!

facts.title: Metals in the Rig Veda
facts.fact: The Rig Veda mentions ayas (metal), likely copper or bronze. This confirms the Vedic period overlapped with the Bronze Age!
facts.shareText: ⚒️ Bronze Age technology confirmed in ancient hymns!

facts.title: Agricultural Calendar
facts.fact: The Rig Veda divides the year into seasons (ritu) and describes planting/harvest times. Ancient agricultural science!
facts.shareText: 🌾 Complete agricultural calendar preserved in poetry!

facts.title: Chariot Engineering
facts.fact: Detailed descriptions of chariot construction appear in hymns - wheel spokes, axles, yokes. Ancient mechanical engineering!
facts.shareText: 🏎️ Chariot blueprints preserved in 3,500-year-old verse!

facts.title: Textile Technology
facts.fact: The Rig Veda mentions weaving, spinning, and dyeing cloth. Complete textile industry preserved in religious poetry!
facts.shareText: 🧵 Ancient textile technology encoded in hymns!

facts.title: The Word 'Yoga'
facts.fact: 'Yoga' (union) comes from the root 'yuj' meaning 'to yoke/join'. The same root gives us 'yoke' and 'junction' in English!
facts.shareText: 🧘 'Yoga' and 'yoke' share the same ancient root!

facts.title: Numbers Are Universal
facts.fact: Sanskrit 'tri' (three) appears in 'triangle', 'tricycle', 'trinity'. The number three has been three forever!
facts.shareText: 3️⃣ 'Three' has been 'tri' for 5,000+ years!

facts.title: The Ancient Word for 'Tooth'
facts.fact: Sanskrit 'danta' (tooth) became 'dental' in English, 'denti' in Italian, 'dent' in French. Teeth have been teeth forever!
facts.shareText: 🦷 'Dental' comes from Sanskrit 'danta' - eternal teeth!

facts.title: Breath of Life
facts.fact: Sanskrit 'prana' (breath/life-force) is related to Latin 'pneuma' and Greek 'pneumon'. Breathing and living were synonymous!
facts.shareText: 🫁 'Prana' (breath) = life itself in ancient wisdom!

facts.title: The King's Word
facts.fact: Sanskrit 'raja' (king) gives us 'royal', 'regal', 'maharaja', and even 'reign'. Kings have ruled the same way for millennia!
facts.shareText: 👑 'Royal' comes from Sanskrit 'raja' (king)!

facts.title: Twelve Adityas
facts.fact: Aditi has twelve sons (Adityas) representing twelve months/aspects of the sun. Divine calendar system!
facts.shareText: ☀️ Twelve sun gods = twelve months - ancient time lords!

facts.title: Agni's Seven Tongues
facts.fact: Agni is described as having seven tongues (flames), each with a specific name. Detailed fire anatomy!
facts.shareText: 👅🔥 Fire has seven tongues, each with its own name!

facts.title: Waters and Soma
facts.fact: Soma is intimately connected with waters (apas) - he's pressed, filtered, and mixed with them. Liquid divinity!
facts.shareText: 💧🍷 Soma and water are inseparable divine liquids!

facts.title: Wind God Vayu
facts.fact: Vayu (Wind) is often paired with Indra - wind clears the path for rain. Meteorological divine duo!
facts.shareText: 💨⚡ Wind and Thunder work together - weather gods unite!

facts.title: The Trinity Prototype
